 Utah Jazz The Utah Jazz are hitting the road on Tuesday night for a matchup against the LA Clippers in hopes that this contest can mark the end of their current 12-game losing streak .

 But in the midst of their action in LA, the Jazz and the Clippers will both be without some key contributors that will shake up the landscape of this game, as revealed in their latest injury reports.

 As has been the case for the last several games, the Jazz will still be without three of their typical starters in this one, along with a key rotation piece in Jaxson Hayes, who will continue to recover from his left knee strain that was suffered this past week.
--> As has been the case for the last several games, the Jazz will still be without three of their typical starters in this one, along with a key rotation piece in Jaxson Hayes, who will continue to recover from his left knee strain that was suffered this past week.
 Lauri Markkanen is still within the four-week recovery timeline from his hand fracture suffered earlier in the month. Jaren Jackson Jr. isn't expected back until December with his MCL tear, and Jusuf Nurkic appears to be trending in the right direction to make his season debut after his preseason foot injury. However, that debut won't be happening on Tuesday night.

 So that continues to leave the Jazz pretty shorthanded in terms of their overall size and big man depth. Utah's starting and backup center will be out for the night, likely leaving Mo Bamba to get his second consecutive start after his 26-point performance from their previous game against the San Antonio Spurs.
